subject: math
title: Fractions, Decimals and Percents
seo_title: Grade 5 Fractions, Decimals and Percents Worksheets with Answer Key (Ontario)
standard_text: Describe relationships and show equivalences among fractions, decimal numbers up to hundredths, and whole-number percents, using appropriate tools and drawings, in various contexts
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on fractions, decimals and percents: hundred grids, 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%, decimals as percents, comparing and ordering, and word problems with test scores and 25% off. 100 questions with an answer key, following the Ontario curriculum.
key_sub: Make an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 10 or 100, then read it as tenths or hundredths. 0.4 = 40%, not 4%, and 1/4 = 0.25, not 0.4.
body_html:
Three ways to show the same amount

A hundred grid has 100 equal squares. The shaded part can be named as a fraction, a decimal or a percent. Percent means out of 100.

Example

40 of 100 squares are shaded. Name the shaded part three ways.

40 out of 100 is 40100. That is 40 hundredths, or 4 tenths.

Answer: 40100 = 0.4 = 40%

Fractions as decimals

Make an equivalent fraction with a denominator of 10 or 100. Multiply the top and bottom by the same number.

DenominatorMultiply byExample
25 (to make 10)12 = 510 = 0.5
52 (to make 10)35 = 610 = 0.6
425 (to make 100)14 = 25100 = 0.25
205 (to make 100)720 = 35100 = 0.35
254 (to make 100)625 = 24100 = 0.24
502 (to make 100)350 = 6100 = 0.06
Example

Write 920 as a decimal and a percent.

20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 920 = 45100.

Answer: 0.45 = 45%

Decimals and percents

Read the decimal as hundredths. 0.4 = 0.40 = 40 hundredths = 40%. 0.07 = 7 hundredths = 7%.

FractionDecimalPercent
120.550%
140.2525%
340.7575%
150.220%
1100.110%
1200.055%
1250.044%

Comparing

Change all the numbers into the same form first. Hundredths are easiest: write each decimal with 2 places.

Example

Order 0.3, 14 and 28% from least to greatest.

0.3 = 0.30. 14 = 0.25. 28% = 0.28. Compare 30, 25 and 28 hundredths.

Answer: 14, 28%, 0.3

25% off

Boots cost $80. They are 25% off. What is the sale price?

25% = 14. 14 of $80 is $20. $80 − $20 = $60.

Answer: $60

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
0.4 = 4%0.4 = 0.40 = 40 hundredths = 40%
14 = 0.4Make hundredths: 14 = 25100 = 0.25
35 = 0.35Make tenths: 35 = 610 = 0.6
8% = 0.88% = 8 hundredths = 0.08
0.65 > 0.7 because 65 > 7Use 2 places: 0.65 < 0.70
25% off $80 means the price is $20$20 is the amount taken off. The sale price is $60.

faq.q: What do Grade 5 students learn about fractions, decimals and percents in Ontario?
faq.a: In the Ontario Grade 5 math curriculum, students show how fractions, decimals to hundredths and whole-number percents are related, using tools like hundred grids and number lines, for example 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%.
No. 1/4 = 25/100 = 0.25 = 25%. The 4 in 1/4 is the number of equal parts, not tenths, so 0.4 is a different number (2/5).

faq.q: How do you change a decimal to a percent?
faq.a: Read the decimal as hundredths. 0.4 = 0.40 = 40 hundredths = 40%, and 0.07 = 7 hundredths = 7%. A common mistake is writing 0.4 as 4%.

faq.q: How do you work out 25% off a price?
faq.a: 25% is 1/4, so divide the price by 4 to find the amount taken off, then subtract. For $80 boots, 1/4 of $80 is $20, so the sale price is $60.

sets.title: Hundred grids: fraction, decimal and percent

items.q: What fraction of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 30 of the 100 squares are shaded, so it is 30100. 70100 is the white part.

items.q: What decimal of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 60 of 100 squares = 60 hundredths = 6 tenths = 0.6. Each full column is one tenth. 0.06 would be only 6 squares, and 0.4 is the white part.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: Percent means out of 100. 45 of 100 squares are shaded, so it is 45%. 55% is the white part.

items.q: What decimal of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 6 of 100 squares = 6 hundredths. Write a 0 in the tenths place: 0.06. 0.6 would be 6 full columns.

items.q: How many squares of a hundred grid would you shade to show 0.6?
items.e: 0.6 = 6 tenths = 60 hundredths, so shade 60 squares (6 full columns). 6 squares would be 0.06.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is shaded?
items.e: 9 of 100 squares are shaded: 9%. 90% would be 9 full columns, and 91% is the white part.

items.q: How many squares of a hundred grid would you shade to show 8%?
items.e: 8% means 8 out of 100, so shade 8 squares. 80 squares would be 80%.

items.q: The whole hundred grid is shaded. What decimal is that?
items.e: 100 out of 100 is the whole grid: 100100 = 1 = 100%. 0.1 is only one column.

items.q: Which shows the shaded part as a decimal and a percent?
items.e: 72 of 100 squares: 72100 = 0.72 = 72%. 0.28 and 28% describe the white part.

items.q: Which does not describe the shaded part?
items.e: 40 of 100 squares: 40100 = 0.4 = 40% = 25. 4% would be only 4 squares.

items.q: What fraction of the hundred grid is shaded, in simplest form?
items.e: 50 of 100 squares = 50100. Divide the top and bottom by 50: 12. Half the grid is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the hundred grid is shaded, in simplest form?
items.e: 25 of 100 squares = 25100. 4 groups of 25 make 100, so it is 14. 34 is the white part.

items.q: How many squares of a hundred grid would you shade to show 25?
items.e: 25 = 40100, so shade 40 squares. 25 just uses the digits 2 and 5, and 60 is the part left white.

items.q: What fraction of the hundred grid is shaded, in simplest form?
items.e: 20 of 100 squares = 20100 = 210 = 15. 2100 would be only 2 squares.

items.q: How many squares of a hundred grid would you shade to show 34?
items.e: 34 = 75100 (multiply the top and bottom by 25), so shade 75 squares. 34 just writes the digits.

items.q: What percent of the hundred grid is not shaded?
items.e: 75 squares are shaded, so 100 − 75 = 25 are white: 25%. 75% is the shaded part.

items.q: What fraction of the grid is shaded, in simplest form?
items.e: 35 of 100 squares = 35100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 720. 35 just uses the digits 3 and 5, and 1320 is the white part.

items.q: Which shows the shaded part three ways?
items.e: 64 of 100 squares: 64100 = 0.64 = 64%. The 36 white squares give 36100, 0.36 and 36%.

items.q: What fraction of the hundred grid is shaded, in simplest form?
items.e: 5 of 100 squares = 5100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 120. 15 is 20 squares, not 5.

items.q: Each grid is one whole. What decimal is shaded in all?
items.e: The first grid is 1 whole. The second has 25 hundredths. 1 + 0.25 = 1.25. 0.25 forgets the full grid.

sets.title: Fractions as decimals: halves to fiftieths

items.q: Write 310 as a decimal.
items.e: 3 tenths: the 3 goes in the tenths place, the first place after the decimal point. 310 = 0.3.

items.q: Write 47100 as a decimal.
items.e: 47 hundredths: the 7 goes in the hundredths place, the second place after the point. 47100 = 0.47.

items.q: Write 8100 as a decimal.
items.e: 8 hundredths: write a 0 in the tenths place to hold it. 8100 = 0.08. 0.8 would be 8 tenths.

items.q: Write 12 as a decimal.
items.e: Multiply the top and bottom by 5: 12 = 510 = 0.5. 0.12 and 1.2 just write the digits of the fraction.

items.q: Write 14 as a decimal.
items.e: 4 × 25 = 100, so multiply the top by 25 too: 14 = 25100 = 0.25. 0.4 is a common mistake: it reads the denominator 4 as tenths.

items.q: Write 0.5 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.5 = 5 tenths = 510. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 12. 15 would be 0.2.

items.q: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 4 equal parts. What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 has 4 equal parts, so each part is 14. The dot is 3 parts along: 34 = 75100 = 0.75. 0.25 is only one part.

items.q: Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: 5 × 2 = 10, so 25 = 410 = 0.4. 0.25 just writes the digits, and 2.5 is 5 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 45 as a decimal.
items.e: 45 = 810 = 0.8. 0.2 is the part that is left, 15.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.4 = 410. Divide the top and bottom by 2: 25. 14 is 0.25, not 0.4.

items.q: Write 15 as a decimal.
items.e: 15 = 210 = 0.2. 0.5 reads the denominator 5 as tenths, the same mistake as 14 = 0.4.

items.q: Write 0.75 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.75 = 75 hundredths = 75100. Divide the top and bottom by 25: 34. 7510 would be 7.5.

items.q: Write 720 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too: 720 = 35100 = 0.35. 0.7 would be 710, and 0.27 adds 7 + 20.

items.q: Write 920 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 920 = 45100 = 0.45. 0.9 would be 910.

items.q: Write 625 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so multiply the top by 4 too: 625 = 24100 = 0.24. 0.6 forgets to multiply, and 0.31 adds 6 + 25.

items.q: Write 1325 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 1325 = 52100 = 0.52. 0.13 forgets to multiply the top by 4.

items.q: Write 350 as a decimal.
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so multiply the top by 2 too: 350 = 6100 = 0.06. 0.6 would be 610.

items.q: Write 2750 as a decimal.
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so 2750 = 54100 = 0.54. 0.27 forgets to multiply the top by 2, and 0.77 adds 27 + 50.

items.q: Write 0.04 as a fraction in simplest form.
items.e: 0.04 = 4 hundredths = 4100. Divide the top and bottom by 4: 125. 410 would be 0.4, and 251 is 25 wholes.

items.q: Write 2 34 as a decimal.
items.e: The 2 wholes stay as 2. 34 = 0.75, so 2 34 = 2.75. 2.3 writes the 3 quarters as 3 tenths.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percent.
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40 hundredths = 40%. 4% is a common mistake: 4% would be 0.04.

items.q: Write 0.07 as a percent.
items.e: 0.07 = 7 hundredths = 7%. 70% would be 0.7.

items.q: Write 0.25 as a percent.
items.e: 0.25 = 25 hundredths = 25%. Multiply by 100: 0.25 × 100 = 25.

items.q: Write 35% as a decimal.
items.e: 35% = 35 hundredths = 0.35. Divide by 100.

items.q: Write 6% as a decimal.
items.e: 6% = 6 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the point: 0.06. 0.6 is 60%.

items.q: Write 12 as a percent.
items.e: 12 = 50100 = 50%. 12% just writes the digits of the fraction.

items.q: Write 14 as a percent.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 25%. 40% reads the denominator 4 as tenths.

items.q: Write 0.9 as a percent.
items.e: 0.9 = 0.90 = 90 hundredths = 90%. 9% would be 0.09.

items.q: Write 0.6 as a percent.
items.e: 0.6 = 0.60 = 60 hundredths = 60%. 40% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 70% as a decimal.
items.e: 70% = 70 hundredths = 7 tenths = 0.7. 0.07 is only 7%.

items.q: Write 50% as a decimal.
items.e: 50% = 50 hundredths = 5 tenths = 0.5. 0.05 is only 5%.

items.q: Write 34 as a percent.
items.e: 34 = 75100 = 75%. 34% just writes the digits, and 25% is only 14.

items.q: Write 0.15 as a percent.
items.e: 0.15 = 15 hundredths = 15%. 150% would be 1.5.

items.q: Write 0.83 as a percent.
items.e: 0.83 = 83 hundredths = 83%. 17% is the part that is left.

items.q: Write 45 as a percent.
items.e: 5 × 20 = 100, so 45 = 80100 = 80%. 45% just writes the digits 4 and 5.

items.q: Write 310 as a percent.
items.e: 310 = 30100 = 30%. 3% would be 3100.

items.q: Write 1 as a percent.
items.e: 1 is one whole, 100 out of 100: 100%. 1% would be 0.01.

items.q: Write 720 as a percent.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 720 = 35100 = 35%. 27% adds 7 + 20.

items.q: Write 925 as a percent.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 925 = 36100 = 36%. 34% adds 9 + 25, and 16% is 25 − 9.

items.q: Write 150 as a percent.
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so 150 = 2100 = 2%. 50% uses the denominator, and 20% would be 15.

sets.title: Compare and order fractions, decimals and percents

items.q: Compare 0.4 and 4%.
items.e: 4% = 0.04. 0.4 = 0.40. 40 hundredths > 4 hundredths, so 0.4 > 4%.

items.q: Compare 0.7 and 0.65.
items.e: 0.7 = 0.70. Compare the tenths: 7 tenths > 6 tenths. So 0.7 > 0.65, even though 65 > 7.

items.q: Compare 0.09 and 0.1.
items.e: 0.1 = 0.10. Compare the tenths: 0 < 1. So 0.09 < 0.1.

items.q: Compare 14 and 0.4.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 0.25. 0.25 < 0.40, so 14 < 0.4. 14 is not 0.4.

items.q: Compare 35 and 0.6.
items.e: 35 = 610 = 0.6. So 35 = 0.6.

items.q: Compare 0.3 and 30%.
Compare 12 and 45%.
items.e: 12 = 50100 = 50%. 50% > 45%, so 12 > 45%.

items.q: Compare 34 and 0.8.
items.e: 34 = 0.75 and 0.8 = 0.80. 75 hundredths < 80 hundredths, so 34 < 0.8.

items.q: Compare 720 and 0.3.
items.e: 720 = 35100 = 0.35. 0.35 > 0.30, so 720 > 0.3.

items.q: Compare 12% and 0.2.

Order from least to greatest:
0.5, 0.45, 0.05, 0.54
items.e: Write them all with 2 places: 0.50, 0.45, 0.05, 0.54. Compare 50, 45, 5 and 54 hundredths. So 0.05, 0.45, 0.5, 0.54.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: As decimals: 34 = 0.75, 0.70, 72% = 0.72, 0.07. The greatest is 34.

items.q: Which is the least?
items.e: As decimals: 18% = 0.18, 0.20, 14 = 0.25, 0.21. The least is 18%.

items.q: The line from 0% to 100% is split into 5 equal parts. What percent is at the red dot?
items.e: 5 equal parts, so each part is 15 = 20%. The dot is 2 parts along: 2 × 20% = 40%. 20% is only one part.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
0.3, 14, 28%
items.e: Make them all decimals: 0.3 = 0.30, 14 = 0.25, 28% = 0.28. So the order is 14, 28%, 0.3.

items.q: Which number is between 0.4 and 0.5?
items.e: 920 = 45100 = 0.45, which is between 0.40 and 0.50. 14 = 0.25, 52% = 0.52 and 0.04 are not.

items.q:
Order from greatest to least:
35, 0.65, 58%
items.e: As decimals: 35 = 0.60, 0.65 and 58% = 0.58. Greatest first: 0.65, 35, 58%.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
52%, 12, 0.48
items.e: As decimals: 52% = 0.52, 12 = 0.50, 0.48. So 0.48, 12, 52%.

items.q:
Order from least to greatest:
45, 0.75, 85%
items.e: As decimals: 45 = 0.80, 0.75, 85% = 0.85. So 0.75, 45, 85%.

items.q: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 20 equal parts. What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: 20 equal parts, so each part is 120 = 0.05. The dot is 7 parts along: 720 = 35100 = 0.35. 0.7 counts the parts as tenths, but there are 20 parts, not 10.

sets.title: Word problems: test scores and 25% off

items.q: Emma scores 18 out of 20 on a spelling test. What percent does she score?
items.e: 1820 = 90100 (multiply the top and bottom by 5) = 90%. 10% is the part she got wrong.

items.q: Noah gets 23 out of 25 on a math quiz. What percent is that?
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 2325 = 92100 = 92%. 23% forgets to multiply by 4, and 8% is the part he missed.

items.q: 15 of the 25 students in a Grade 5 class are going on a field trip. What percent of the class is going?
items.e: 1525 = 60100 = 60%. 40% is the part of the class that is not going.

items.q: A pair of winter boots costs $80. The store takes 25% off. How much money is taken off?
items.e: 25% = 14. 14 of $80 is $80 ÷ 4 = $20. $60 is the sale price, and $25 confuses 25% with $25.

items.q: A hockey stick costs $40. It is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 25% = 14, and 14 of $40 is $10. The sale price is $40 − $10 = $30. $10 is only the amount taken off, and $15 takes away $25 instead of 25%.

items.q: A T-shirt costs $30. It is 10% off. What is the sale price?
items.e: 10% = 110. 110 of $30 is $3. $30 − $3 = $27. $20 takes away $10 instead of 10%.

items.q: Store A has 14 off a pair of skates. Store B has 20% off the same skates. Which store takes off more?
items.e: 14 = 25%, and 25% > 20%. The skates cost the same to start with, so Store A takes off more.

items.q: On a science test, Mateo scores 21 out of 25 and Hana scores 17 out of 20. Who has the higher percent?
items.e: 2125 = 84100 = 84%. 1720 = 85100 = 85%. 85% > 84%, so Hana did better, even with fewer marks.

items.q: At one school, 0.7 of the students stay for lunch. The rest go home for lunch. What percent go home?
items.e: 0.7 = 70% stay. All the students are 100%, so 100% − 70% = 30% go home.

items.q: In a Grade 5 class, 35 of the students walk to school. What percent of the class walk?
items.e: 35 = 60100 = 60%. 35% just writes the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: The forecast says there is a 75% chance of snow tomorrow. What fraction is that?
items.e: 75% = 75100. Divide the top and bottom by 25: 34. 14 is the chance that it does not snow.

items.q: There is a 75% chance of snow tomorrow. What is the chance that it does not snow, as a decimal?
items.e: Snow or no snow makes 100%. 100% − 75% = 25% = 0.25. 0.75 is the chance of snow.

items.q: A hockey team won 12 of its 20 games this season. What percent of its games did it win?
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 1220 = 60100 = 60%. 40% is the games it did not win.

items.q: Two maple syrup jugs are the same size. Jug A is 14 full. Jug B is 0.4 full. Which jug has more syrup?
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 0.25. 0.4 = 0.40. 0.40 > 0.25, so Jug B has more. Watch out: 14 is not 0.4.

items.q: Ethan’s tablet battery shows 45%. What fraction of a full charge is that, in simplest form?
items.e: 45% = 45100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 920. 1120 is the part that is empty.

items.q: Sofia has 1 m of ribbon. She uses 0.35 m for a craft. What fraction of the metre is left, in simplest form?
items.e: 1 − 0.35 = 0.65 m is left. 0.65 = 65100 = 1320 (divide by 5). 720 is the part she used.

items.q: A loonie ($1) is shared equally among 4 friends. How much does each friend get?
items.e: $1 ÷ 4 = 14 of a dollar = 25100 = $0.25 = 25¢. 40¢ is the mistake 14 = 0.4.

items.q: 50 students from one school run in the Terry Fox Run. 41 of them run the whole 5 km. What percent run the whole 5 km?
items.e: 50 × 2 = 100, so 4150 = 82100 = 82%. 41% forgets to multiply by 2, and 18% is the part that did not run the whole way.

items.q: On a reading test, Olivia gets 1720 of the questions right, Jayden gets 0.8 of them right and Amira gets 82%. Who has the highest score?
items.e: Make them all percents: 1720 = 85100 = 85%, 0.8 = 80%, and 82%. 85% is the highest, so Olivia.

items.q: A quiz has 20 questions. Nathan gets 0.75 of them right. How many questions does he get right?
items.e: 0.75 = 34, and 34 of 20 is 20 ÷ 4 × 3 = 15 questions. 5 is the number he gets wrong, and 7.5 multiplies by 10 instead of 20.
